narrative: New England beat PIT 20-3. The offense posted -0.07 EPA/play (41% success rate) while the defense allowed -0.36 EPA/play. Turnover margin was 0.

good: The defense was suffocating: held Pittsburgh to a field goal and forced no red-zone touchdowns on their one trip, while the unit allowed just 2 third-down conversions on 12 attempts.
Rhamondre Stevenson was the game's most valuable Patriot, delivering in the clutch moments that swung win probability.
bad: The offense sputtered relative to league norms: converted just 4 of 12 third downs (well below the 40% standard) and scored TDs on only 1 of 3 red-zone trips instead of the typical 55%.
Clock management continues to haunt this team—the coaching staff has already acknowledged two straight games with questionable decisions late in the second quarter.
ugly: Negative EPA per play on offense is a long-term concern masquerading as a win—this defensive performance papered over some real offensive inefficiency.

playerOfTheGame.reason: Led the team with +3% win probability added.

fanTake: Well, that's more like it. The Patriots absolutely dominated the Steelers at home, 20-3, in a performance that felt like a genuine defensive masterclass—holding Pittsburgh scoreless in the touchdown department while our offense churned out two scores and two field goals. Rhamondre Stevenson was the architect of the win, delivering 3% win probability added when it mattered most. The defense was genuinely excellent, allowing negative 0.36 EPA per play, which is well above the standard. The only real sting is that our offense generated negative 0.07 EPA per play—not bad by any stretch, but a reminder that we're still searching for consistency on that side of the ball.
